newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Bullish T-bonds seen growing hesitant.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Bullish T-bonds seen growing hesitant.

text.p: The bullish U.S. Treasury bond futures market is likely to grow somewhat hesitant in the near term, even though it has continued to defy predictions of a major pullback, technical analysts said.

"The trend is certainly to higher prices," said Stewart Taylor, president of Taylor Consulting. "The problem with the market right now is that it is extremely, extremely overbought. We don't, at this point, want to buy strength."
He, as well as other analysts, warned against trying to pick a top and going short, but recommended keeping the powder keg dry for an opportunity to buy at lower levels.
"At some point here, maybe even from today's high, you're going to get a fairly significant correction," Taylor said.
September T-bonds rallied early in the session after a weaker than expected June consumer price index, pausing briefly at Friday's 114-15/32 high and then ratcheting further up toward midsession.

David Ging, a vice president at Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette, saw the market probing the 115-1/4 area before putting in a top. That target was projected by assuming the current rally from late-June lows would achieve gains similar to those in the April-May upleg and the May-June advance.
Taylor noted that the move from the April lows on the daily chart showed a clear five-wave sequence from an Elliott Wave standpoint.
But it was difficult to project a target for the current leg, the fifth wave, due to a murky picture in its subdivided wave count, he said.

"The subdivisions in the last wave are unclear," he said. "We should be pretty close to having completed it (the larger five-wave move), but the wave count on the hourly from the last low -- it's just hard to say if it has or not."
Taylor also said a series of cycle highs were due very soon and a relatively subdued performance in municipal bond index futures might be another negative signal.

"One thing that happens quite often is that at market highs, there's a divergence between Treasury bonds and the muni bonds," he said. "I'm looking at that as a non-confirmation of this last round of strength."
Until today's rally, September muni bond futures had not been able to take out their mid-June highs. The contract rallied sharply today, however, up 24/32 at 120-8/32 early in the afternoon.
